Volcanic Eruption Map Spotlight: Anak Krakatau, Indonesia

2026-09-06 IQAir Staff Writers Anak Krakatau, volcano, Indonesia, Sunda Strait, eruption, volcanic ash, air quality, mapping, Pacific Ring of Fire, aviation
Read the source article

Quick summary

Anak Krakatau volcano in Indonesia's Sunda Strait erupted on September 4, 2026, sending ash plumes to 50,000 feet, disrupting 300+ flights, and prompting evacuation zones and air quality monitoring via interactive maps.

Key takeaways

  • Anak Krakatau began erupting on September 4, 2026, producing lava fountains and ash plumes reaching approximately 50,000 feet
  • The volcano is at Alert Level III (second-highest on Indonesia's four-level scale)
  • Over 300 flights were affected, with airports in Jakarta, Bandung, and Lampung disrupted
  • Authorities established a 3-kilometer exclusion zone around the active crater
  • Indonesia's disaster mitigation agency plans cloud seeding to encourage rainfall that may help remove ash from affected areas
